messages:
Arjun Desai: quick schema bikeshed we should settle today 🙏

Arjun Desai: in the draft profile schema we currently have both `profile_id` and `profile_ref` floating around. what do we want to standardize on for v1?

Arjun Desai: use case split in my head:
- registry/storage needs a stable identifier
- route config needs “what to enable” (and ideally pinned / deterministic)

Arjun Desai: also: how are we representing HW constraints? right now i have a `hardware_constraints` object in notes but not sure if we want “gpu_sku allowlist” vs “capability constraints”.

Quentin Harris: +1 to settling this.

Quentin Harris: from model registry POV, I strongly prefer:
- `profile_id`: immutable identifier (string, could be uuid OR a canonical name)
- `profile_version`: semver-ish (or monotonically increasing int)

Quentin Harris: then “ref” is a derived thing you can pass around like `model_id + profile_id + profile_version`.

Quentin Harris: reason: refs tend to grow aliases (`latest`, `recommended`) and that’s where determinism dies unless we’re super careful.

Jonas Weber: +1 on determinism. eval harness gating wants to compare baseline vs *exact* artifacts.

Jonas Weber: if we allow `recommended` as a ref, it has to resolve to a concrete version before it hits runtime, and ideally we log the resolved one.

Benji Okafor: control plane angle: we need one field in route config. naming matters bc it’ll show up in APIs + Console.

Benji Okafor: I’m leaning `quantization_profile_ref` as the route config field (string). We can accept a “friendly” token, but we should STORE resolved (pinned) value.

Benji Okafor: i.e. user requests `recommended`, backend resolves to `…/v3` and persists that.

Jordan Lee: yes please. policy engine needs deterministic inputs.

Jordan Lee: allowing “moving targets” in persisted config is a footgun. if we support aliases, they should be request-time only.

Karthik Iyer: Applied ML preference: make it human readable.

Karthik Iyer: UUIDs are painful in docs/support. something like:
- `profile_id`: `int8-w8a16-calib_rwinograd` (ok maybe not that ugly but you get it)
- `profile_version`: `1.0.0`

Karthik Iyer: and we include `artifacts_digest` / `artifact_uri` for the runtime to verify.

Selene Huang: re: HW constraints — we need enough structure to *block* unsafe enablement.

Selene Huang: minimum set IMO:
- allowed GPU families/classes (A100/H100/L4/etc)
- min CUDA / driver (maybe optional for v1)
- any sequence-length caps (we’ve seen regressions at long context)
- known caveats (KV cache interaction, etc) as a freeform note

Selene Huang: would rather not do “compute capability math” in the first cut unless runtime/policy really needs it.

Quentin Harris: agree. also “GPU SKU allowlist” is easiest for compatibility matrix and for docs.

Quentin Harris: compute capability is attractive but then you get edge cases (new SKU shares CC but different mem/bw).

Jonas Weber: HW constraints also ties to perf suite. we’ll want to bucket by SKU class anyway.

Jonas Weber: for the schema, can we do something like:
- `hardware_allowlist`: `a100-80gb`, `h100-sxm`, `l40s`
- `min_vram_gb`: 80 (optional)

Jonas Weber: and maybe `notes` for “tested on” vs “supported on”.

Arjun Desai: ok, sounds like:
1) schema has `profile_id` + `profile_version` (and maybe `status`: experimental/stable/deprecated)
2) route config uses `quantization_profile_ref` as the field name
3) aliases like `recommended` are API sugar but persist resolved pinned ref

Arjun Desai: question: do we want the persisted ref to be a single string (like `qpl://<model>/<variant>/<profile_id>@<version>`) or separate fields?

Benji Okafor: single string is simplest for APIs + Console, but we can parse/validate.

Benji Okafor: separate fields is nicer for migrations but more moving parts.

Jordan Lee: single string is fine if we enforce a strict format + validator (no silent parsing magic).

Quentin Harris: registry side, I’d like to avoid inventing a new URI scheme unless it buys us something.

Quentin Harris: maybe simplest: `quantization_profile_ref` = `<model_id>:<variant>:<profile_id>:<profile_version>`.

Quentin Harris: (and we can always display it prettier in Console)

Karthik Iyer: +1. also we should not overload `profile_id` with model info if ref already includes model+variant.

Selene Huang: for HW constraints, I propose we start with:
- `supported_gpu_skus`: list of strings
- `max_context_tokens_tested`: int (or range)
- `incompatible_features`: list (e.g., “speculative_decode”, “fp8_kv_cache”) if needed

Selene Huang: even if policy doesn’t use all of it on day 1, it’s useful for audit + guardrails.

Jonas Weber: careful with `max_context_tokens_tested` vs “supported”. could be misread.

Jonas Weber: maybe:
- `max_context_tokens_supported`
- `max_context_tokens_tested`

Jonas Weber: but we can keep one for v1 and be explicit in docs.

Arjun Desai: makes sense. v1 probably:
- `supported_gpu_skus` (explicit allowlist)
- `max_context_tokens` (as a hard cap for compatibility)
- `notes` / `known_caveats`

Arjun Desai: and we can expand later.

Quentin Harris: 👍. one more thing: naming.

Quentin Harris: in schema, I’d avoid `profile_ref` entirely to reduce confusion. only keep `profile_id` + `profile_version`.

Quentin Harris: `profile_ref` exists only in APIs/config as `quantization_profile_ref`.

Benji Okafor: +1. reduces “which one do i put where” questions.

Jordan Lee: +1. also easier to write a deterministic resolver: (route ref) -> (registry entry) -> (artifact digest).

Arjun Desai: ok I’ll update the draft:
- remove `profile_ref` from schema
- standardize route config field name `quantization_profile_ref`
- HW constraints: `supported_gpu_skus` + `max_context_tokens` + `min_vram_gb` (optional) + `known_caveats`

Arjun Desai: will ping w/ updated snippet for review later today.

Selene Huang: please include a field that can drive automatic blocks (even if it’s just `max_context_tokens`). that’s the big one.

Jonas Weber: and include `artifacts_digest` in the schema. makes eval artifacts & runtime checks much easier.

Arjun Desai: yep. adding `artifacts_digest` + `calibration_set_ref` as well.

Karthik Iyer: :thumbsup: once you have a draft, I’ll sanity check naming from ML side.

Quentin Harris: thanks. once it’s updated I’ll align with validator expectations in registry.

Benji Okafor: +1, and I’ll make sure control plane can store the ref + the resolved “applied profile” in audit logs.

Jordan Lee: 👍 please also note in the doc: aliases resolve at write-time, not read-time.

Arjun Desai: will do.
